Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (Horizon CTO), Ethan Cole (ML Engineer), Priya Nair (Security Ops), Alex Kim (Product)

Summary (auto):  Intro discovery: path to first token + hosting options. Technical Q&A on latency and security. Action items captured.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me are Ravi and Liam from our SE team. How are you folks doing?
[00:12] Sofia (Horizon): Good, thanks. Excited to dig in — we want a clear path to get a prototype in our analytics UI next sprint.
[00:20] Ethan (Horizon): Yep, we're most worried about interactive latency; users run short queries and expect snappy responses.
[00:28] Maya: Great. High-level, we have three common paths: Hosted (fastest time-to-first-token, self-serve with free credits), Dedicated (reserved capacity for predictable throughput), and Private/VPC or on-prem for strict data residency. Which ones are you leaning toward?
[00:42] Sofia: For the POC we want Hosted to move fast, but we'll need to validate security posture. If that goes well, we might move to Dedicated or a VPC later.
[00:51] Priya (Horizon): Right, security questions: SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO — SAML specifically. Also, data residency for EU customers.
[01:05] Ravi (Redwood SE): Totally fair. For Hosted we provide SOC2 artifacts and audit logs; KMS integration is supported on Dedicated and Private, and Hosted has encryption in transit and at rest with provider-managed keys — we can discuss bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options for Private.
[01:22] Alex (Horizon): Any gotchas on throughput or cost for interactive workloads?
[01:27] Liam (Redwood SE): The tradeoff is latency vs cost. For sub-200ms tail latency you'll often pick smaller batches, more pins to a lower-sequence model, or a dedicated pool. For many UIs, a smart prefix caching strategy and async token streaming hits the sweet spot.
[01:44] Ethan: Can you explain prefix caching? I saw KV cache in docs but want the simple layman's version.
[01:50] Ravi: Sure — imagine repeated context (like the user's product spec) being kept in memory so subsequent requests reuse the stored key-values instead of recomputing. It trims per-token compute. Sometimes speech-to-text transcriptions can show K-V cash in older exports — sorry about that, docs can be noisy.
[02:03] Sofia: Ha, we saw that in an earlier doc yes.
[02:06] Priya: For compliance we will need a list of what is retained, retention windows, and the audit trail. Also whether Redwood can sign a DPA with data processing addenda.
[02:18] Maya: We can share a compliance packet — SOC2 summary, pen test summary, DPA template. I'll attach those.
[02:25] Sofia: Timeline — we're aiming for a demo of the assistant in two sprints, so about 3 weeks. Is that realistic for Hosted?
[02:33] Maya: Absolutely. With free credits and the quickstart app you can be at first token within a day, and a simple UI integration within a week. The 3-week demo with some latency tuning is reachable.
[02:44] Ethan: What's the typical path to the first real request in prod? We have infra standards, auth, and feature flags to think about.
[02:51] Ravi: Most teams do: 1) Redeem free credits and spin up the quickstart (we'll send a starter repo), 2) Swap in your prompt sets and sample logs, 3) Run a small benchmark against Redwood hosted endpoints, 4) If throughput or residency requires it, move to Dedicated or Private and we help size the GPU pools.
[03:08] Alex: Are there SDKs? We use Node + Python stacks.
[03:12] Maya: Yes, official SDKs for Node and Python, and a simple REST surface. We also have examples for streaming responses and function/tool calling.
[03:19] Ethan: For the benchmark, what metrics should we capture?
[03:22] Ravi: Latency P50/P95/P99, token cost per request, throughput (requests/sec), error rates, and output quality metrics against a labeled set. We'll share a template.
[03:33] Priya: On SSO — is SAML supported for the console and user access? We need SSO for team logins.
[03:38] Maya: Yes, SAML-based SSO and SCIM provisioning for user management are supported for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we support SSO for enterprise accounts via SAML; we'll share the integration doc.
[03:50] Ethan: How about model choice — we plan to use an LLaMA-style baseline, any recommendations on quantization levels?
[03:57] Ravi: For interactive UI, 4-bit or 8-bit quantization can reduce memory and cost but we often recommend validating quality. We'll provide quantization profiles per model; in-hosted we surface recommended variants that trade latency and cost.
[04:12] Sofia: Competitors — are you seeing folks run into surprises when migrating from OpenAI or Vertex?
[04:18] Liam: Migrating can reveal differences in tokenization, prompt construction, and output variance. We help with small eval suites and regression checks. Also routing and fallback policies prevent downtime if a model variant is overloaded.
[04:30] Speaker 1: Sorry — quick Q, backup for on-prem — do you support air-gapped?
[04:35] Ravi: Yes, we have a Private on-prem package that can be deployed into air-gapped environments; it requires some ops collaboration but is supported for enterprise contracts.
[04:44] Maya: For the POC, we'll focus Hosted. I'll send the credits and quickstart repo. If you hit throughput or data residency blockers, we'll look at Dedicated sizing.
[04:55] Ethan: What about observability? We need token-level billing for product owners.
[04:59] Liam: Our Console shows per-route token breakdowns, latency trails, and tracing hooks. You can export logs to your logging stack and we provide retention add-ons.
[05:10] Priya: Audit logs — detail level? We need admin actions and API keys activity.
[05:15] Ravi: We capture admin actions, model rollouts, and API key usage. For Dedicated/Private you can extend retention windows and forward logs to your SIEM.
[05:25] Sofia: Ok, let's talk success criteria: For this POC we want P95 under 500ms on common queries, cost under $X per 1k requests (we'll provide X), and acceptable accuracy on our intent classifier.
[05:43] Maya: Good explicit targets. Send those numbers and sample logs; we'll baseline against Hosted and come back with recommendations.
[05:52] Ethan: One more — is there a way to pin model versions for canaries?
[05:56] Liam: Yes, version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies are built-in — you can pin at route-level and set traffic splits.
[06:05] Alex: Any prebuilt prompts or eval harnesses?
[06:08] Ravi: We have a lightweight eval harness and example prompt library; also can integrate with your internal A/B eval pipeline.
[06:15] Maya: Alright, let's capture next steps. I'll share the credits + quickstart repo and the compliance packet. Ravi and Liam will share the benchmark template and a suggested schedule for a SE-led deep dive next week.
[06:31] Sofia: Sounds good. We'll try to redeem credits today and run the quickstart.
[06:36] Maya: Perfect. Anything else?
[06:39] Priya: Please include the DPA template and a short note on KMS support in Hosted — whether BYOK is supported or only Dedicated/Private.
[06:50] Maya: Noted — I'll clarify BYOK in the packet.
[06:54] Ethan: Thanks everyone, excited to get going.
[06:57] Maya: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up via email with the artifacts and calendar invite for the deep dive.
[07:05] (call ends)

Recap (auto): Redwood to send (1) free credits + quickstart repo, (2) SOC2/DPA/compliance packet, (3) benchmarking template and pilot plan. Horizon to send sample logs and success criteria. Schedule SE deep dive after initial benchmark.

End of transcript.
